title: Cost Harbor: policy adapter and mini-batcher defaults for tenant-friendly unit-econ
author: Ava Chen
description: Context: We observed recurring tenant-level unit-econ regressions when autoscaling and batch-routing heuristics chose overly large batch shapes or aggressive quantization tiers for low-SLA tenants. This PR introduces 'Cost Harbor' — a lightweight policy adapter that evaluates tenant budget/latency classes at the gateway and applies conservative mini-batcher defaults and quant-tier caps before requests reach the scheduler. Motivation: reduce tail regressions and unexpected unit-cost spikes for cost-sensitive tenants without changing global batcher behavior. Scope: 1) gateway policy adapter service (inline library + small HTTP hook) 2) new tenant-default presets: mini-batcher shapes, max-quant-tier, safe-prefill window 3) CLI preview tool (redwood cost-harbor preview) to dry-run policy decisions against tenant sample traces 4) telemetry hooks and unit-econ regression alerts. Checklist: - [x] design doc and simulation (link: Linear ENG-7812) - [x] implementation of policy adapter and integration tests - [x] CLI preview with dry-run mode and CSV output - [x] e2e smoke test against local scheduler - [x] observability dashboard (cost-harbor tenant view) Summary of commits: - feat(policy): add cost-harbor adapter and config schema - feat(cli): add redwood cost-harbor preview command with sample replay - feat(runtime): apply mini-batcher hints to scheduler admission - fix(test): deterministic sample harness for preview tests - infra: add cost-harbor dashboard panels and alert rules High level files touched: - gateway/policies/cost_harbor.go (new) - cli/cost_harbor_preview/main.go (new) - scheduler/mini_batcher_hints.go (mod) - configs/defaults/cost_harbor_presets.yaml (new) - telemetry/dashboards/cost_harbor.json (new) - integrations/testdata/tenant-sample-small.json (new) Testing and CI: Unit tests cover policy evaluation matrix (budget x latency class x workload shape). Integration tests run a 50-tenant micro-sim and assert mean unit-cost reduction for budgeted tenants or no more than 5% latency regression for high-SLA tenants. CI flake: an early run failed due to a race in the preview harness — fixed by adding deterministic seeding. Runtime performance: applying the adapter adds ~120us median overhead at gateway (measured in local perf run) but reduces high-cost tail events by 18% in the synthetic tenant mix. Rollout plan: - Canary on dedicated staging region for two days with tenants flagged via feature-flag - Monitor unit-econ dashboard and alert thresholds for regressions - Gradual 25% -> 50% -> 100% rollouts pending no alerts Observability/telemetry: emits policy.apply, policy.decision, policy.fallback metrics and a per-tenant unit-cost delta metric emitted when adapter is active. Added Grafana panels to show tenant distribution and sample dry-run comparisons. Backwards compatibility and fallback: adapter uses config-driven safe-fallbacks (no-op) if scheduler rejects hints; it will never increase batch size or request higher quant tiers than requested. Security notes: adapter config stored in tenant config store with RBAC: only infra/admin roles can modify presets. Known limitations and follow-ups: - Prefill heuristics currently conservative for multi-model requests; follow-up to incorporate model-level cost signatures (ENG-7890) - CLI preview needs a richer sampling UI (future PR) Release notes: - Introduces Cost Harbor gateway policy adapter which applies conservative mini-batcher and quant-tier defaults for budgeted tenants - Adds redwood cost-harbor preview CLI for dry-run verification - Adds telemetry and dashboards to monitor unit-econ impact Impact: Expected to reduce unexpected cost spikes for budgeted tenants and provide operators a lower-risk knob for tenant defaults. Merge notes: squash-merged into main. Links: Linear ENG-7812 (design), Linear ENG-7890 (follow-up), SUP-4432 (support ticket that motivated change).
discussion: Diego Morales (reviewer): Left a few comments on the scheduler hints — we should ensure hints are advisory and not mandatory. Suggested adding explicit fallback metrics.
Ava Chen (author): Addressed via a fallback path in scheduler/mini_batcher_hints.go and added policy.fallback metric. Pushed fixup commit and added unit tests for fallback.
Priya Nair (reviewer): Ran CLI preview locally, found a CSV formatting issue for empty traces, requested a test. Ava pushed a small patch and updated tests. Approved after fixes.
release_notes:
- Cost Harbor gateway policy adapter: conservative mini-batcher and quant-tier defaults for budgeted tenants
- redwood cost-harbor preview CLI (dry-run)
- Telemetry panels and alerts for adapter impact
notes_for_ops: Canary with feature flag 'cost-harbor:enabled' per-region. Watch metric 'policy.fallback' and per-tenant unit-cost delta. Rollback by disabling feature flag or removing adapter config. Ensure RBAC for config edits.
manual_steps_documented:
1) To run preview locally: ./bin/redwood cost-harbor preview --tenant-sample integrations/testdata/tenant-sample-small.json --out results.csv
2) To enable adapter: set feature flag and apply configs/defaults/cost_harbor_presets.yaml via tenant-config API
3) Troubleshooting: if scheduler rejects hints, check scheduler logs for 'hint-rejected' events and inspect policy.fallback metric.
risk_summary: Low-medium. Correctness risk is mitigated by making hints advisory and conservative presets. Main risk is incomplete model-level signatures; follow-ups planned. Runtime overhead is small (~120us).
notes_for_release_manager: Include the cost-harbor dashboard in the platform release. Coordinate canary start time with on-call SRE and Product. Attach ENG-7812 in release notes.
